statement: Stating how many files a metric read is not the same as stating what it examined when those files hand work elsewhere. B3 read every CI workflow and said so, but a workflow that calls a reusable workflow in another repository or runs a local action delegates its test and lint commands to code Cejel never opens, so the certificate read as if those commands were absent. Rule: when a read file can delegate to content outside the read set, count the delegations it names and state them as not read beside the read count; count only references that really run something (a ./ path with no action.yml is not an action), and add nothing at zero so the common case stays byte-identical.

A presentation-only read added inside a scored collector can still move a status, because a read failure there is attributed to whichever signal scope is active and can abstain a metric that never depended on the file. Re-read only files a signal already read unconditionally, under that same signal, with the same guard and read path, so attribution is a set no-op and the skip count is deduplicated; never read under a signal whose own reads short-circuit (a .some over files reads only up to the first match). Prove it with a before/after dump of full reports across every corpus specimen and rubric, not only with fingerprints, which exclude labels and cannot see the line you added.
